The Prophet's wives went out at night to relieve themselves; Umar, wanting them veiled, called out to Sauda, Allah revealed the veil verses, and the Prophet let them go out.
After Khaibar was conquered the Prophet chose Safiya, whose husband had been killed, married her on the way with a wedding meal of Hais, and helped her mount his camel.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives in verse 66:4 and tells how the Prophet kept away from his wives twenty-nine days, then offered them a choice.
When one wife broke a bowl of food sent by another, the Prophet gathered the food, kept the broken bowl and sent back an unbroken one.
Um Salama's group of wives asked that gifts reach the Prophet in any wife's house; he said revelation came to him only in Aisha's bed, and Aisha silenced Zainab.
Maimuna was told giving her slave-girl to her maternal uncles would have earned more than freeing her; the Prophet drew lots among his wives, and Sauda gave Aisha her turn.
The Prophet drew lots among his wives for journeys and gave each a day and night, and Sauda gave hers to Aisha.
Returning from Khaibar, the Prophet marries Safiya, holds a wedding feast without meat or bread, and veils her, marking her as one of his wives rather than a slave.
Told to give his wives a choice, the Prophet starts with Aisha, who chooses Allah and His Messenger; verses also concern Zainab and Zaid and setting aside a wife's turn.
Aisha and Hafsa plot over the honey the Prophet drank at Zainab's; Umar names them the two wives who backed each other and recounts the Prophet's seclusion and plain life.
The Prophet had nine wives, giving night turns to eight and going round all in one night; Ibn Abbas urges marriage, as the nation's best had the most wives.
Aisha, after Khaula offers herself and the verse on postponing wives' turns comes, says the Prophet's Lord hastens to please him; Ibn Abbas says the Prophet married in Ihram.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives in verse 66:4 and tells of the Prophet's twenty-nine days away from his wives, his bare room, and the option verses.
The Prophet swore to stay away from his wives for a month, sat in his upper room, and returned after twenty-nine days, saying the month can be twenty-nine days.
The Prophet drew lots among his wives for journeys, kept turns and died in Aisha's house; a virgin bride gets seven days, a matron three; Umar cautioned Hafsa about Aisha.
Making one's wife unlawful is not divorce; the Prophet's wives played a trick, claiming a bad smell, until he gave up honey, and verses of Surah 66 came down.
Umar names Aisha and Hafsa as the two wives who backed each other against the Prophet, telling of his warnings and the Prophet's twenty-nine days in his upper room.
When Aisha and Hafsa agreed to say he smelled of Maghafir, the Prophet swore off the honey he drank at Zainab's, and verses 66.1-4 were revealed.
When the Prophet stayed long with Hafsa drinking honey, Aisha had Sauda and Safiya say he smelled of Maghafir, a trick that made him refuse the honey thereafter.
Zainab boasted Allah married her to the Prophet from above seven heavens; the verse on what the Prophet hid concerned her and Zaid, and the Hijab verse concerned her.
